title.zh: 卷九十三 志第四十二: 食貨一
title.raw: 卷九十三 志第四十二: 食貨一 Volume 93 Treatises 46: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 食貨一

translations.literal: Food and Commodities I
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics I

sentences.zh: 《洪範》八政，食為首而貨次之，蓋食貨者養生之源也。

translations.literal: In the Hong Fan, among the Eight Policies, food comes first and commodities second—for food and commodities are the source of sustaining life.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong Fan lists eight policies of government, with food first and wealth second, because grain and goods are the foundation on which life itself depends.

sentences.zh: 民非食貨則無以為生，國非食貨則無以為用。

translations.literal: Without food and commodities the people have no means to live; without food and commodities the state has no means to function.
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot survive without grain and goods, and the state cannot govern without them.

sentences.zh: 是以古之善治其國者，不能無取於民，亦未嘗過取於民，其大要在乎量入為出而已。

translations.literal: Therefore those of antiquity who governed their states well could not avoid taking from the people, yet they never took excessively; the great principle lay simply in measuring income before expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers who governed well still had to levy taxes, but they never overtaxed; their cardinal rule was to match spending to revenue.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「生財有大道，生之者眾，食之者寡，為之者疾，用之者舒。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "There is a great Way to producing wealth: many produce it, few consume it, those who make it are swift, those who use it are slow."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "There is a great principle of wealth: let many create it, let few consume it, let production be vigorous, and let expenditure be leisurely."

sentences.zh: 此先王理財之道也。

translations.literal: This was the former kings' Way of managing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fiscal wisdom of the sage kings of old.

sentences.zh: 後世則不然，以漢、唐、宋觀之，當其立國之初，亦頗有成法，及數傳之後，驕侈生焉，往往取之無度，用之無節。

translations.literal: Later ages were not so. Observing Han, Tang, and Song, when they first founded their states they also had fairly established laws; after several generations, arrogance and extravagance arose, and they often took without measure and spent without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties did otherwise. In Han, Tang, and Song alike, sound fiscal laws existed at the founding, but after a few reigns luxury set in and rulers took without limit and spent without restraint.

sentences.zh: 於是漢有告緡、算舟車之令，唐有借商、稅間架之法，宋有經、總制二錢，皆掊民以充國，卒之民困而國亡，可嘆也已。

translations.literal: Thus Han had the denunciation of hidden wealth and taxation of boats and carriages; Tang had borrowing from merchants and the room-frame tax; Song had the Jing and Zongzhi levies—all squeezing the people to fill the state, until in the end the people were distressed and the state perished. Lamentable indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Han then imposed the informer laws and taxes on boats and carriages; Tang exacted loans from merchants and the room-frame levy; Song created the Jing and Zongzhi surcharges—all wringing the people to fill the treasury until the people were ruined and the realm fell. A lamentable end.

sentences.zh: 元初，取民未有定制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, levies on the people had no fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuan, taxation of the populace had not yet been standardized.

sentences.zh: 及世祖立法，一本於寬。

translations.literal: When Shizu legislated, he took leniency as his single foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai Khan codified the law, he grounded it entirely in moderation.

sentences.zh: 其用之也，於宗戚則有歲賜，於凶荒則有賑恤，大率以親親愛民為重，而尤惓惓於農桑一事，可謂知理財之本者矣。

translations.literal: In his spending, to kinsmen of the imperial clan there were annual grants; in famine and disaster there was relief—generally he valued cherishing kin and loving the people, and was especially earnest about agriculture and sericulture. He may be said to have known the root of managing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His expenditures included annual gifts to the imperial clan and relief in times of famine, always prioritizing kinship and care for the people, with special devotion to farming and sericulture. He truly understood the foundation of sound finance.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗語中書省臣曰：「凡賜與雖有朕命，中書其斟酌之。」

translations.literal: Shizu once told the ministers of the Secretariat: "Though every grant bears my command, the Secretariat should weigh and adjust it."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai once told the Secretariat: "Even when I order a grant, you must exercise your own judgment in dispensing it."

sentences.zh: 成宗亦嘗謂丞相完澤等曰：「每歲天下金銀鈔幣所入幾何？

translations.literal: Chengzong also once said to the Chancellor Wanze and others: "Each year, how much gold, silver, and paper currency does the realm take in?
translations.idiomatic: Temür Khan likewise asked Chancellor Wanze and his colleagues: "How much gold, silver, and paper money does the empire collect each year?

sentences.zh: 諸王駙馬賜與及一切營建所出幾何？

translations.literal: How much goes out in grants to princes and imperial sons-in-law and in all construction?
translations.idiomatic: How much goes out in gifts to princes and imperial sons-in-law and in all building projects?

sentences.zh: 其會計以聞。」

translations.literal: Present the accounts and report to me."
translations.idiomatic: Compile the accounts and report them to me."

sentences.zh: 完澤對曰：「歲入之數，金一萬九千兩，銀六萬兩，鈔三百六十萬錠，然猶不足於用，又於至元鈔本中借二十萬錠矣。

translations.literal: Wanze replied: "Annual receipts are 19,000 taels of gold, 60,000 taels of silver, and 3,600,000 ingots of paper money—yet still insufficient for use; we have also borrowed 200,000 ingots from the Zhiyuan note reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Wanze answered: "Annual revenue is nineteen thousand taels of gold, sixty thousand taels of silver, and three million six hundred thousand ingots of paper money—yet it still falls short, and we have already borrowed two hundred thousand ingots from the Zhiyuan note reserve.

sentences.zh: 自今敢以節用為請。」

translations.literal: From now on I venture to request frugality in expenditure."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth I beg Your Majesty to practice economy in spending."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his counsel.

sentences.zh: 世稱元之治以至元、大德為首者，蓋以此。

translations.literal: The age praises the Yuan's governance, ranking the Zhiyuan and Dade eras foremost—largely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Historians rank the Zhiyuan and Dade reigns as the high point of Yuan rule—and this is largely why.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，國用寖廣。

translations.literal: From that time onward, state expenditure gradually expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, state spending steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 除稅糧、科差二者之外，凡課之入，日增月益。

translations.literal: Apart from grain tax and corvée levies, every category of revenue increased day by day and month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the grain tax and corvée assessments, every other levy rose month after month.

sentences.zh: 至於天歷之際，視至元、大德之數，蓋增二十倍矣，而朝廷未嘗有一日之蓄，則以其不能量入為出故也。

translations.literal: By the Tianli era, compared with the Zhiyuan and Dade figures, revenue had increased roughly twentyfold—yet the court never had a single day's reserve, because it could not measure income against expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianli period revenue had grown some twentyfold over the Zhiyuan and Dade levels, yet the court never held even a day's surplus—because it refused to match spending to income.

sentences.zh: 雖然，前代告緡、借商、經總等制，元皆無之，亦可謂寬矣。

translations.literal: Even so, the former dynasties' systems of denunciation, merchant loans, Jing and Zongzhi levies—the Yuan had none of these. It may still be called lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the Yuan never adopted such measures as Han's informer laws, Tang's merchant loans, or Song's Jing and Zongzhi surcharges, and in that sense remained comparatively mild.

sentences.zh: 其能兼有四海，傳及百年者，有以也夫。

translations.literal: That it could hold all within the Four Seas and pass down a century—there was reason for this indeed.
translations.idiomatic: That it could rule the empire and endure a century had its reasons.

sentences.zh: 故仿前史之法，取其出入之制可考者：一曰經理，二曰農桑，三曰稅糧，四曰科差，五曰海運，六曰鈔法，七曰歲課，八曰鹽法，九曰茶法，十曰酒醋課，十有一曰商稅，十有二曰市舶，十有三曰額外課，十有四曰歲賜，十有五曰俸秩，十有六曰常平義倉，十有七曰惠民藥局，十有八曰市糴，十有九曰賑恤，具著於篇，作《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Therefore, following the method of former histories, we take those systems of revenue and expenditure that can be verified: first, land registration; second, agriculture and sericulture; third, grain tax; fourth, corvée levies; fifth, sea transport; sixth, paper currency; seventh, annual levies; eighth, salt monopoly; ninth, tea monopoly; tenth, wine and vinegar tax; eleventh, commercial tax; twelfth, maritime trade; thirteenth, supplementary levies; fourteenth, annual grants; fifteenth, salaries and ranks; sixteenth, ever-normal and charity granaries; seventeenth, public medicine bureaus; eighteenth, government grain purchases; nineteenth, relief and succor—all set forth in full in this chapter, composing the Treatise on Food and Commodities.
translations.idiomatic: Following the practice of earlier histories, we record every verifiable system of revenue and expenditure: land registration, agriculture and sericulture, grain tax, corvée levies, sea transport, paper currency, annual levies, the salt monopoly, the tea monopoly, wine and vinegar duties, commercial tax, maritime trade, supplementary levies, annual grants, salaries, ever-normal and charity granaries, public medicine bureaus, government grain purchases, and relief—all treated in this Treatise on Finance and Economics.

sentences.zh: ○經理

translations.literal: ○ Land Registration
translations.idiomatic: ○ Land Registration and Survey

sentences.zh: 經界廢而後有經理，魯之履畝，漢之核田，皆其制也。

translations.literal: After the field-boundary system was abandoned came land registration; Lu's foot-measurement of fields and Han's verification of fields were both of this type.
translations.idiomatic: Land surveys arose only after field boundaries fell into disuse; Lu's foot-measurement of fields and Han's land verification were earlier forms of the same institution.

sentences.zh: 夫民之強者田多而稅少，弱者產去而稅存，非經理固無以去其害；

translations.literal: The strong among the people hold much land yet pay little tax; the weak lose their property yet tax remains—without land registration there is no way to remove this harm.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful held vast estates yet paid little tax, while the weak lost their land yet still owed dues—without a land survey there was no remedy for such abuses.

sentences.zh: 然經理之制，苟有不善，則其害又將有甚焉者矣。

translations.literal: Yet if the land-registration system is poorly executed, its harm may become even greater still.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a poorly conducted survey could inflict harm worse than the disease it was meant to cure.

sentences.zh: 仁宗延祐元年，平章章閭言：「經理大事，世祖已嘗行之，但其間欺隱尚多，未能盡實。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renzong's Yanyou reign, Grand Councilor Zhang Min said: "Land registration is a major undertaking; Shizu had already carried it out once, but concealment and fraud remained widespread and the registration could not be made fully true.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renzong's Yanyou reign, Grand Councilor Zhang Min said: "Land registration is a major undertaking; Shizu had already carried it out once, but concealment and fraud remained widespread and the registration could not be made fully true.

sentences.zh: 以熟田為荒地者有之，懼差而析戶者有之，富民買貧民田而仍其舊名輸稅者亦有之。

translations.literal: Some reported fertile fields as wasteland; some split households for fear of levies; some wealthy households bought poor people's land yet paid tax under the old name.
translations.idiomatic: Some reported fertile fields as wasteland; some split households for fear of levies; some wealthy households bought poor people's land yet paid tax under the old name.

sentences.zh: 由是歲入不增，小民告病。

translations.literal: Thus annual revenue did not rise and common people complained of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Thus annual revenue did not rise and common people complained of hardship.

sentences.zh: 若行經理之法，俾有田之家，及各位下、寺觀、學校、財賦等田，一切從實自首，庶幾稅入無隱，差徭亦均。」

translations.literal: If the land-registration method is carried out, so that households with land—and fields of princely estates, monasteries, schools, and fiscal properties—altogether confess truthfully, then tax revenue may be without concealment and corvée levies made even."
translations.idiomatic: If the land-registration method is carried out, so that households with land—and fields of princely estates, monasteries, schools, and fiscal properties—altogether confess truthfully, then tax revenue may be without concealment and corvée levies made even."

sentences.zh: 於是遣官經理。

translations.literal: Thereupon officials were dispatched to conduct the registration.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon officials were dispatched to conduct the registration.

sentences.zh: 以章閭等往江浙，尚書你咱馬丁等往江西，左丞陳士英等往河南，仍命行御史臺分臺鎮遏，樞密院以軍防護焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Min and others were sent to Jiang-Zhe; Minister Nizhamading and others to Jiangxi; Left Vice Chancellor Chen Shiying and others to Henan; traveling branches of the Branch Censorate were also ordered to hold the districts in check, and the Privy Council supplied troops for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Min and others were sent to Jiang-Zhe; Minister Nizhamading and others to Jiangxi; Left Vice Chancellor Chen Shiying and others to Henan; traveling branches of the Branch Censorate were also ordered to hold the districts in check, and the Privy Council supplied troops for protection.

sentences.zh: 其法先期揭榜示民，限四十日，以其家所有田，自實於官。

translations.literal: The law first posted proclamations to inform the people, setting a limit of forty days within which each household was to report its own holdings to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The law required advance public notice, then gave households forty days to declare all their land to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 或以熟為荒，以田為蕩，或隱占逃亡之產，或盜官田為民田，指民田為官田，及僧道以田作弊者，並許諸人首告。

translations.literal: Whether one reported fertile land as waste, fields as marsh, concealed property of fugitives, stole official land as private land, claimed private land as official land, or monks and Daoists cheated with land—all were permitted to be denounced by anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who reported fertile land as waste, fields as marshland, concealed fugitives' property, seized official land as private, mislabeled private land as official, or monks and Daoists who falsified holdings was subject to denunciation.

sentences.zh: 十畝以下，其田主及管幹佃戶皆杖七十七。

translations.literal: For ten mu or less, the landowner and the managing tenant were each beaten seventy-seven strokes.
translations.idiomatic: For holdings of ten mu or less, both the landowner and the managing tenant received seventy-seven strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 二十畝以下，加一等。

translations.literal: For twenty mu or less, one degree was added to the penalty.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty mu or less, the penalty increased by one degree.

sentences.zh: 一百畝以下，一百七；

translations.literal: For one hundred mu or less, one hundred and seven strokes;
translations.idiomatic: For one hundred mu or less, one hundred and seven strokes;

sentences.zh: 以上，流竄北邊，所隱田沒官。

translations.literal: above that, exile to the northern frontier, and the concealed land confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: above that, exile to the northern frontier and confiscation of the concealed land.

sentences.zh: 郡縣正官不為查勘，致有脫漏者，量事論罪，重者除名。

translations.literal: If the chief officials of prefecture and county failed to investigate and verify, causing omissions, guilt was assessed according to circumstances; in serious cases they were removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county magistrates who failed to investigate and allowed omissions were punished according to circumstances; in serious cases they were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 此其大略也。

translations.literal: This is the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general scheme.

sentences.zh: 然期限猝迫，貪刻用事，富民黠吏，並緣為奸，以無為有，虛具於籍者，往往有之。

translations.literal: Yet the deadline was suddenly pressed, greedy and harsh officials held power, wealthy households and cunning clerks all seized the opportunity for fraud—declaring what did not exist, falsely entering items in the register—this often occurred.
translations.idiomatic: But the deadline was brutally short, greedy officials held sway, and wealthy families and cunning clerks colluded in fraud, inventing holdings and entering phantom acreage in the registers.

sentences.zh: 於是人不聊生，盜賊並起，其弊反有甚於前者。

translations.literal: Thus people could not make a living, bandits rose together, and the harm in fact exceeded what had gone before.
translations.idiomatic: The people could barely survive, banditry spread, and the abuse proved worse than the evils the survey was meant to end.

sentences.zh: 仁宗知之，明年，遂下詔免三省自實田租。

translations.literal: Renzong understood this; the next year he issued an edict exempting the three provinces from rent on self-declared fields.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong understood the problem and the following year exempted the three provinces from rent on self-declared land.

sentences.zh: 二年，時汴梁路總管塔海亦言其弊，於是命河南自實田，自延祐五年為始，每畝止科其半，汴梁路凡減二十二萬餘石。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Bianliang Circuit intendant Ta Hai also spoke of these abuses; thereupon Henan self-declared fields, from the fifth year of Yanyou onward, were taxed at only half per mu; Bianliang Circuit altogether was reduced by more than 220,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Bianliang intendant Ta Hai reported the same abuses, and Henan self-declared fields from the fifth year of Yanyou were taxed at half rate, reducing Bianliang Circuit's levy by more than 220,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 至泰定、天歷之初，又盡革虛增之數，民始獲安。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Taiding and Tianli reigns, inflated figures were entirely abolished, and the people at last found peace.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taiding and Tianli reigns phantom acreage was finally purged from the registers, and the people at last found relief.

sentences.zh: 今取其數之可考者，列於後云：

translations.literal: Now we take the figures that can be verified and list them below:
translations.idiomatic: Verifiable figures are listed below:

sentences.zh: 河南省，總計官民荒熟田一百一十八萬七百六十九頃。

translations.literal: Henan Province: in total official, private, waste, and fertile fields, 1,180,769 qing.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Province: a total of 1,180,769 qing of official, private, waste, and fertile land.

sentences.zh: 江西省，總計官民荒熟田四十七萬四千六百九十三頃。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Province: in total 474,693 qing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Province: a total of 474,693 qing.

sentences.zh: 江浙省，總計官民荒熟田九十九萬五千八十一頃。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe Province: in total 995,081 qing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe Province: a total of 995,081 qing.

sentences.zh: ○農桑

translations.literal: ○ Agriculture and Sericulture
translations.idiomatic: ○ Agriculture and Sericulture

sentences.zh: 農桑，王政之本也。

translations.literal: Agriculture and sericulture are the root of royal government.
translations.idiomatic: Farming and sericulture are the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 太祖起朔方，其俗不待蠶而衣，不待耕而食，初無所事焉。

translations.literal: Taizu rose in the northern frontier; their custom was to clothe themselves without waiting for silkworms and to eat without waiting to plow—at first they had no concern for such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan rose on the northern steppe, where people clothed themselves without sericulture and fed themselves without tillage, and at first paid such matters no heed.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位之初，首詔天下，國以民為本，民以衣食為本，衣食以農桑為本。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's accession, he first issued an edict to all under Heaven: the state takes the people as its foundation; the people take food and clothing as their foundation; food and clothing take agriculture and sericulture as their foundation.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign Kublai issued his first edict to the realm: the state rests on the people, the people rest on food and clothing, and food and clothing rest on farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 於是頒《農桑輯要》之書於民，俾民崇本抑末。

translations.literal: Thereupon he promulgated the book Essentials of Agriculture and Sericulture among the people, causing them to honor the root and restrain the branch.
translations.idiomatic: He then distributed the Essentials of Agriculture and Sericulture to the people, urging them to honor productive labor and restrain speculation.

sentences.zh: 其睿見英識，與古先帝王無異，豈遼、金所能比哉？

translations.literal: His sagacious vision and brilliant understanding were no different from the ancient sage kings—how could Liao and Jin be compared?
translations.idiomatic: His wisdom matched that of the sage kings of antiquity—how could the Liao or Jin dynasties compare?

sentences.zh: 中統元年，命各路宣撫司擇通曉農事者，充隨處勸農官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, each circuit pacification commission was ordered to select persons versed in farming to serve as local agriculture promotion officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, each circuit pacification commission was ordered to select persons versed in farming to serve as local agriculture promotion officials.

sentences.zh: 二年，立勸農司，以陳邃、崔斌等八人為使。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Agriculture Promotion Office was established, with Chen Sui, Cui Bin, and six others as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the Agriculture Promotion Office was established, with Chen Sui, Cui Bin, and six others as commissioners.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，立司農司，以左丞張文謙為卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Agriculture Commission was established, with Left Vice Chancellor Zhang Wenqian as its director.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Agriculture Commission was established, with Left Vice Chancellor Zhang Wenqian as its director.

sentences.zh: 司農司之設，專掌農桑水利。

translations.literal: The Agriculture Commission was charged exclusively with agriculture, sericulture, and waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: The Agriculture Commission was charged exclusively with agriculture, sericulture, and waterworks.

sentences.zh: 仍分布勸農官及知水利者，巡行郡邑，察舉勤惰。

translations.literal: Agriculture promotion officials and hydrology experts were also stationed across prefectures and counties to tour the districts and report diligence and sloth.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture promotion officials and hydrology experts were also stationed across prefectures and counties to tour the districts and report diligence and sloth.

sentences.zh: 所在牧民長官提點農事，歲終第其成否，轉申司農司及戶部，秩滿之日，注於解由，戶部照之，以為殿最。

translations.literal: Local chiefs overseeing the people were to supervise farming; at year's end achievements were ranked and reported to the Agriculture Commission and the Ministry of Revenue; upon completion of a term of office, the record was entered on the certificate of release, and the Ministry of Revenue consulted it to determine superior and inferior performance.
translations.idiomatic: Local magistrates supervised farming; at year's end achievements were ranked and reported to the Agriculture Commission and the Ministry of Revenue, and upon completion of a term the record was entered on the certificate of release for the Ministry of Revenue to use in judging performance.

sentences.zh: 又命提刑按察司加體察焉。

translations.literal: The Investigation and Surveillance Commissions were also ordered to conduct additional inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The Investigation and Surveillance Commissions were also ordered to conduct additional inspection.

sentences.zh: 其法可謂至矣。

translations.literal: The regulations may be said to have reached their fullest measure.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations may be said to have reached their fullest measure.

sentences.zh: 是年，又頒農桑之制一十四條，條多不能盡載，載其所可法者：縣邑所屬村疃，凡五十家立一社，擇高年曉農事者一人為之長。

translations.literal: That year he also promulgated fourteen regulations on agriculture and sericulture; many cannot all be recorded—those that may serve as models are recorded: in villages under counties and districts, for every fifty households one community was established, choosing one elder knowledgeable in farming as its head.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he issued fourteen regulations on agriculture and sericulture. Not all can be quoted here; the essential provisions were these: every fifty households in a village formed a community, headed by an elder versed in farming.

sentences.zh: 增至百家者，別設長一員。

translations.literal: When increased to one hundred households, a separate head was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Communities of one hundred households received an additional head.

sentences.zh: 不及五十家者，與近村合為一社。

translations.literal: Those with fewer than fifty households joined with a nearby village to form one community.
translations.idiomatic: Villages with fewer than fifty households merged with a neighbor into one community.

sentences.zh: 地遠人稀，不能相合，各自為社者聽。

translations.literal: Where the land was remote and people sparse and combination was impossible, they were permitted to form communities on their own.
translations.idiomatic: In sparsely settled regions where merger was impractical, separate communities were permitted.

sentences.zh: 其合為社者，仍擇數村之中，立社長官司長以教督農民為事。

translations.literal: Where communities were combined, among several villages a community head and ward head were still chosen, whose business was to teach and supervise the farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Merged communities still chose community and ward heads from among the villages to instruct and supervise farming.

sentences.zh: 凡種田者，立牌橛於田側，書某社某人於其上，社長以時點視勸誡。

translations.literal: All who planted fields set markers at the field's edge, inscribing such-and-such community and person upon them; the community head inspected and exhorted on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Every farmer posted a marker at the field edge bearing the community name and his own; the community head inspected on schedule and offered guidance.

sentences.zh: 不率教者，籍其姓名，以授提點官責之。

translations.literal: Those who did not follow instruction had their names registered and handed to the supervising official for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who defied instruction had their names recorded and reported to the supervising official for punishment.

sentences.zh: 其有不敬父兄及凶惡者，亦然。

translations.literal: Those who were disrespectful to parents and elders or vicious and wicked were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied to those who were unfilial or habitually violent.

sentences.zh: 仍大書其所犯於門，俟其改過自新乃毀，如終歲不改，罰其代充本社夫役。

translations.literal: Their offenses were still written large upon their doors; only when they reformed and renewed themselves were these destroyed. If by year's end they did not reform, they were punished by being made to perform the community's corvée in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Their offenses were posted in large characters on their doors and removed only after reform; if they failed to reform within the year, they were compelled to perform the community's corvée labor in others' stead.

sentences.zh: 社中有疾病凶喪之家不能耕種者，眾為合力助之。

translations.literal: If within a community a household with illness, death, or mourning could not farm, the multitude joined strength to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: When illness or bereavement prevented a household from farming, the community pooled labor to help.

sentences.zh: 一社之中災病多者，兩社助之。

translations.literal: If illness and disaster were many in one community, two communities assisted.
translations.idiomatic: If one community suffered widespread sickness, a second community joined in the relief.

sentences.zh: 凡為長者，復其身，郡縣官不得以社長與科差事。

translations.literal: All who served as heads were exempted in person; prefectural and county officials might not assign corvée duties to community heads.
translations.idiomatic: Community heads were personally exempt from corvée, and local officials might not assign them levy duties.

sentences.zh: 農桑之術，以備旱暵為先。

translations.literal: In the arts of agriculture and sericulture, guarding against drought came first.
translations.idiomatic: The first principle of farming and sericulture was preparedness against drought.

sentences.zh: 凡河渠之利，委本處正官一員，以時浚治。

translations.literal: All benefit of rivers and canals was entrusted to one local chief official to dredge and maintain on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Each locality assigned one chief official to dredge and maintain irrigation works on schedule.

sentences.zh: 或民力不足者，提舉河渠官相其輕重，官為導之。

translations.literal: Where popular strength was insufficient, the canal commissioner assessed severity and the state directed the work.
translations.idiomatic: Where the people lacked labor, the canal commissioner assessed the need and the government directed the work.

sentences.zh: 地高水不能上者，命造水車。

translations.literal: Where the land was high and water could not reach, they were ordered to build waterwheels.
translations.idiomatic: Where high ground kept water from reaching the fields, farmers were ordered to build waterwheels.

sentences.zh: 貧不能造者，官具材木給之。

translations.literal: Those too poor to build them—the state supplied timber and materials.
translations.idiomatic: The poor who could not afford them received timber and materials from the government.

sentences.zh: 俟秋成之後，驗使水之家，俾均輸其直。

translations.literal: After the autumn harvest, households that used the water were verified and made to pay the cost equally.
translations.idiomatic: After the autumn harvest, households that benefited shared the cost equally.

sentences.zh: 田無水者鑿井，井深不能得水者，聽種區田。

translations.literal: Fields without water were to dig wells; where wells were dug deep yet could not reach water, they were permitted to plant compartment fields.
translations.idiomatic: Fields without irrigation were to dig wells; where wells failed to reach water, farmers might plant compartment fields instead.

sentences.zh: 其有水田者，不必區種。

translations.literal: Those with irrigated fields need not plant compartment fields.
translations.idiomatic: Irrigated fields were exempt from compartment planting.

sentences.zh: 仍以區田之法，散諸農民。

translations.literal: The method of compartment fields was still distributed among the farmers.
translations.idiomatic: The compartment-field method was still distributed among farmers as a drought remedy.

sentences.zh: 種植之制，每丁歲種桑棗二十株。

translations.literal: Planting regulations: each adult male annually planted twenty mulberry and jujube trees.
translations.idiomatic: Planting regulations required each adult male to plant twenty mulberry and jujube trees each year.

sentences.zh: 土性不宜者，聽種榆柳等，其數亦如之。

translations.literal: Where the soil was unsuitable, they were permitted to plant elm, willow, and the like in the same numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Where the soil was unsuitable, elm, willow, or similar trees might be substituted in equal number.

sentences.zh: 種雜果者，每丁十株，皆以生成為數，願多種者聽。

translations.literal: For miscellaneous fruit trees, ten per adult male, all counted by surviving growth; those wishing to plant more were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: For miscellaneous fruit trees, ten per adult male were required, counted by surviving growth; additional planting was permitted.

sentences.zh: 其無地及有疾者不與。

translations.literal: Those without land or with illness were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Landless persons and the ill were exempt.

sentences.zh: 所在官司申報不實者，罪之。

translations.literal: Local officials who reported falsely were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who filed false reports were punished.

sentences.zh: 仍令各社布種苜蓿，以防饑年。

translations.literal: Each community was still ordered to sow alfalfa against years of famine.
translations.idiomatic: Each community was also required to sow alfalfa as insurance against famine.

sentences.zh: 近水之家，又許鑿池養魚並鵝鴨之數，及種蒔蓮藕、雞頭、菱角、蒲葦等，以助衣食。

translations.literal: Households near water were further permitted to dig ponds to raise fish and flocks of geese and ducks, and to plant and cultivate lotus root, gorgon fruit, water chestnut, cattail, reed, and the like to supplement food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Households near water might dig ponds for fish and poultry and cultivate lotus, gorgon fruit, water chestnut, cattail, and reed to supplement their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 凡荒閑之地，悉以付民，先給貧者，次及余戶。

translations.literal: All waste and idle land was entirely given to the people—the poor first, then the remaining households.
translations.idiomatic: All waste land was granted to the people, the poor receiving priority and others following.

sentences.zh: 每年十月，令州縣正官一員，巡視境內，有蟲蝗遺子之地，多方設法除之。

translations.literal: Every year in the tenth month, one chief official of prefecture and county was ordered to tour the jurisdiction; wherever locust eggs remained, every means was devised to eliminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Each October a chief local official toured the district and used every available means to destroy locust eggs wherever found.

sentences.zh: 其用心周悉若此，亦仁矣哉！

translations.literal: That their care was so thorough and complete—how benevolent indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Such thorough and humane attention to the people's welfare was truly benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 九年，命勸農官舉察勤惰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, agricultural promotion officials were ordered to investigate diligence and sloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, agricultural commissioners were ordered to report diligence and neglect.

sentences.zh: 於是高唐州官以勤升秩，河南陜縣尹王仔以惰降職。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Gaotang prefectural official was promoted in rank for diligence; Wang Zai, magistrate of Shan County in Henan, was demoted for sloth.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaotang prefect was promoted for diligence, while Wang Zai, magistrate of Shan County in Henan, was demoted for neglect.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲申明其制。

translations.literal: From this time each year the regulations were reissued.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the regulations were reissued annually.

sentences.zh: 十年，令探馬赤隨處入社，與編民等。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, tammaqchi were ordered to enter communities wherever they were, equal with registered civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, imperial guardsmen were required to join local communities on equal footing with registered civilians.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，立行大司農司及營田司於江南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the traveling Grand Secretariat of Agriculture and the Colonization Bureau were established in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, the traveling Grand Secretariat of Agriculture and the Colonization Bureau were established in the south.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，頒農桑雜令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, miscellaneous regulations on agriculture and sericulture were promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, supplementary agricultural regulations were issued.

sentences.zh: 是年，又以江南長吏勸課擾民，罷其親行之制，命止移文諭之。

translations.literal: That year, because Jiangnan senior officials' personal promotion of farming disturbed the people, the system of personal execution was abolished; they were ordered only to issue written instructions.
translations.idiomatic: That year, because southern officials' personal farm inspections harassed the people, direct supervision was abolished in favor of written instructions alone.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以勸農司並入各道肅政廉訪司，增僉事二員，兼察農事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Agricultural Promotion Bureau was merged into each circuit's Surveillance and Investigation Commission, with two additional vice commissioners to oversee agricultural affairs jointly.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, the Agricultural Promotion Bureau was merged into each circuit's Surveillance Commission, with two additional vice commissioners to oversee farming.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，又命提調農桑官帳冊有差者，驗數罰俸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year, it was further ordered that agricultural officials whose account books were deficient should have salaries deducted according to the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year, agricultural officials whose records fell short had their salaries docked accordingly.

sentences.zh: 故終世祖之世，家給人足。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout Shizu's reign, every household had enough and every person was provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Thus throughout Kublai's reign every household had enough and every person was provided for.

sentences.zh: 天下為戶凡一千一百六十三萬三千二百八十一，為口凡五千三百六十五萬四千三百三十七，此其敦本之明效可睹也已。

translations.literal: Under Heaven there were altogether 11,633,281 households and 53,654,337 persons—the clear effect of honoring the root is visible here.
translations.idiomatic: The realm registered 11,633,281 households and 53,654,337 persons—the visible fruit of honoring productive labor.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德元年，罷妨農之役。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengzong's Dade reign, labor corvées that obstructed farming were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Temür's Dade reign, corvée duties that interfered with farming were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十一年，申擾農之禁，力田者有賞，遊惰者有罰，縱畜牧損禾稼桑棗者，責其償而後罪之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the prohibition on disturbing farming was reiterated; those who worked fields diligently were rewarded, the idle and lazy were punished; those who let livestock damage grain, mulberry, and jujube were made to compensate before being punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the ban on disturbing farming was renewed: diligent farmers were rewarded, the idle were punished, and those whose livestock damaged crops or trees were required to compensate before facing punishment.

sentences.zh: 由是大德之治，幾於至元。

translations.literal: Thus the governance of the Dade reign nearly matched that of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Dade reign therefore nearly matched the prosperity of the Zhiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 然旱暵霖雨之災叠見，饑毀薦臻，民之流移失業者亦已多矣。

translations.literal: Yet drought and flood disasters appeared in succession, famine and ruin arrived repeatedly, and those among the people who drifted away and lost their livelihoods were already many.
translations.idiomatic: Yet droughts and floods came in succession, famine followed famine, and many people were displaced and lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，淮西廉訪僉事苗好謙獻種蒔之法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuzong's Zhida reign, Miao Haoqian, vice commissioner of the Huaixi Surveillance Commission, presented a method of planting and cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuzong's Zhida reign, Miao Haoqian, vice commissioner of the Huaixi Surveillance Commission, submitted a planting scheme.

sentences.zh: 其說分農民為三等，上戶地一十畝，中戶五畝，下戶二畝或一畝，皆築垣墻圍之，以時收采桑椹，依法種植。

translations.literal: His proposal divided farmers into three grades: upper households ten mu of land, middle households five mu, lower households two or one mu—all enclosed with earthen walls, harvesting mulberry fruit on schedule and planting according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: His plan divided farmers into three grades: upper households received ten mu, middle five, lower two or one—all enclosed by earthen walls for scheduled mulberry harvest and regulated planting.

sentences.zh: 武宗善而行之。

translations.literal: Wuzong approved and implemented it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong approved the plan and put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 其法出《齊民要術》等書，茲不備錄。

translations.literal: The method came from books such as the Qimin Yaoshu; it is not fully recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The method drew on works such as the Essential Techniques for the Common People and is not reproduced here in full.

sentences.zh: 三年，申命大司農總挈天下農政，修明勸課之令，除牧養之地，其餘聽民秋耕。

translations.literal: In the third year, an order was reiterated commanding the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture to oversee all agricultural administration under Heaven, clarify promotion and inspection regulations, exempt pasturelands, and permit the people to conduct autumn plowing on the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture was ordered to oversee farming empire-wide, enforce promotion regulations, exempt pasturelands, and allow autumn plowing elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 仁宗皇慶二年，復申秋耕之令，惟大都等五路許耕其半。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renzong's Huangqing reign, the autumn-plowing order was reiterated; only in the five circuits of Dadu and the like was half-plowing permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Renzong's Huangqing reign, autumn plowing was ordered again, though in the Dadu region and four other circuits only half the land might be plowed.

sentences.zh: 蓋秋耕之利，掩陽氣於地中，蝗蝻遺種皆為日所曝死，次年所種，必盛於常禾也。

translations.literal: The benefit of autumn plowing lies in burying yang energy in the earth; locust eggs and surviving pests are all killed by the sun's heat, and grain planted the following year necessarily flourishes beyond ordinary crops.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn plowing traps warmth in the soil, exposes locust eggs and pest larvae to the sun, and yields a stronger harvest the following year.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，以好謙所至，植桑皆有成效，於是風示諸道，命以為式。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou, wherever Haoqian had gone mulberry planting all proved effective; thereupon instructions were sent to all circuits, ordering his method to serve as the model.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanyou, wherever Haoqian had worked mulberry planting succeeded, and his method was proclaimed as the model for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，令各社出地，共蒔桑苗，以社長領之，分給各社。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, each community was ordered to set aside land jointly to cultivate mulberry seedlings, led by the community head and distributed to each community.
translations.idiomatic: That November each community was required to set aside communal land for mulberry seedlings, managed by the community head and distributed among members.

sentences.zh: 四年，又以社桑分給不便，令民各畦種之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because distributing community mulberry was inconvenient, the people were ordered each to plant in their own plots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year communal mulberry distribution proved impractical, and households were ordered to plant in their own plots instead.

sentences.zh: 法雖屢變，而有司不能悉遵上意，大率視為具文而已。

translations.literal: Though the law changed repeatedly, officials could not fully follow the imperial intent; generally they treated it as empty formality.
translations.idiomatic: Though regulations changed repeatedly, officials failed to follow imperial intent and treated them as mere formalities.

sentences.zh: 五年，大司農司臣言：「廉訪司所具栽植之數，書於冊者，類多不實。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, ministers of the Grand Secretariat of Agriculture said: "The planting figures furnished by the Surveillance Commissions and entered in the registers are mostly untrue."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Grand Secretariat reported: "The planting figures furnished by the Surveillance Commissions and entered in the registers are mostly untrue."

sentences.zh: 觀此，則惰於勸課者，又不獨有司為然也。

translations.literal: Seeing this, those slack in promoting farming were not officials alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus negligence in agricultural promotion was not confined to officials alone.

sentences.zh: 致和之後，莫不申明農桑之令。

translations.literal: After the Zhihe era, none failed to reissue agricultural regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhihe era, agricultural regulations were reissued in every reign.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，各道廉訪司所察勤官內丘何主簿等凡六人，惰官濮陽裴縣尹等凡四人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, the Surveillance Commissions of each circuit reported diligent officials such as Registrar He of Neiqiu—six in all—and slack officials such as Magistrate Pei of Puyang—four in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianli, surveillance commissioners reported six diligent officials, including Registrar He of Neiqiu, and four negligent ones, including Magistrate Pei of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 其可考者，蓋止於此云。

translations.literal: What can be verified probably ends here.
translations.idiomatic: Verifiable records probably end here.

sentences.zh: ○稅糧

translations.literal: ○ Grain Tax
translations.idiomatic: ○ Grain Tax

sentences.zh: 元之取民，大率以唐為法。

translations.literal: The Yuan's levies on the people generally followed Tang law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan taxation generally followed Tang models.

sentences.zh: 其取於內郡者，曰丁稅，曰地稅，此仿唐之租庸調也。

translations.literal: What was taken from inner circuits was called poll tax and land tax—this imitated Tang's zu, yong, and diao.
translations.idiomatic: In the interior they levied poll tax and land tax, modeled on the Tang zu-yong-diao system.

sentences.zh: 取於江南者，曰秋稅，曰夏稅，此仿唐之兩稅也。

translations.literal: What was taken from Jiangnan was called autumn tax and summer tax—this imitated Tang's two-tax system.
translations.idiomatic: In the south they levied autumn and summer taxes, modeled on the Tang two-tax system.

sentences.zh: 丁稅、地稅之法，自太宗始行之。

translations.literal: The methods of poll tax and land tax began to be implemented under Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Poll and land taxes were first implemented under Ögedei Khan.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗每戶科粟二石，後又以兵食不足，增為四石。

translations.literal: At first Taizong levied two shi of grain per household; later, because military provisions were insufficient, it was increased to four shi.
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei initially levied two shi of grain per household, then raised it to four when military stores ran short.

sentences.zh: 至丙申年，乃定科征之法，令諸路驗民戶成丁之數，每丁歲科粟一石，驅丁五升，新戶丁驅各半之，老幼不與。

translations.literal: In the bingshen year, the method of assessment was fixed: each circuit verified the number of adult males per household; each adult male annually paid one shi of grain, each bond servant five sheng, new households and bond servants half each; the old and young were not included.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingshen year rates were fixed: each adult male paid one shi of grain annually, bond servants five sheng, new households and bond servants half each, with the old and young exempt.

sentences.zh: 其間有耕種者，或驗其牛具之數，或驗其土地之等征焉。

translations.literal: Among them, those who farmed might be assessed by the number of oxen and tools, or by the grade of their land.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers might be assessed by livestock and tools or by land grade.

sentences.zh: 丁稅少而地稅多者納地稅，地稅少而丁稅多者納丁稅。

translations.literal: Where poll tax was less and land tax more, land tax was paid; where land tax was less and poll tax more, poll tax was paid.
translations.idiomatic: Households paid whichever levy was higher, poll tax or land tax.

sentences.zh: 工匠僧道驗地，官吏商賈驗丁。

translations.literal: Artisans, monks, and Daoists were assessed by land; officials, merchants, and traders by adult males.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans, monks, and Daoists were assessed on land; officials and merchants on adult males.

sentences.zh: 虛配不實者杖七十，徒二年。

translations.literal: False allocation not matching reality: seventy strokes of the staff, two years penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: False registration brought seventy strokes of the staff and two years of penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 仍命歲書其數於冊，由課稅所申省以聞，違者各杖一百。

translations.literal: They were still ordered annually to record the numbers in registers, reported by the tax office to the province and thence announced; violators each received one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Annual registers were required, reported through tax offices to the province; violators received one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 逮及世祖，申明舊制，於是輸納之期、收受之式、關防之禁、會計之法，莫不備焉。

translations.literal: When this reached Shizu, the old system was clarified; then periods of payment, forms of receipt, checkpoint prohibitions, and accounting methods were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai clarified the old system, completing payment schedules, receipt procedures, checkpoint rules, and accounting methods.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，遠倉之糧，命止於沿河近倉輸納，每石帶收腳錢中統鈔三錢，或民戶赴河倉輸納者，每石折輸輕賫中統鈔七錢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, grain for distant granaries was ordered paid only at granaries along rivers; for each shi an additional three qian of Zhongtong notes was collected as transport fee, or households delivering to river granaries might pay seven qian of light-load Zhongtong notes per shi in lieu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong, distant deliveries were limited to riverside granaries, with three qian transport fee per shi, or seven qian in lieu for direct delivery.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔僧、道、也裏可溫、答失蠻、儒人凡種田者，白地每畝輸稅三升，水地每畝五升。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict: monks, Daoists, Nestorian Christians, Muslims, and Confucian scholars who farmed paid three sheng per mu of dry land and five sheng per mu of irrigated land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year monks, Daoists, Nestorians, Muslims, and scholars who farmed paid three sheng per mu of dry land and five of irrigated land.

sentences.zh: 軍、站戶除地四頃免稅，余悉征之。

translations.literal: Military and courier households were exempt on four qing of land; the remainder was fully taxed.
translations.idiomatic: Military and courier households were tax-exempt on four qing; all other land was taxed.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，詔窎戶種田他所者，其丁稅於附籍之郡驗丁而科，地稅於種田之所驗地而取。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, registered households farming elsewhere paid poll tax in their registered circuit by adult males and land tax where they farmed by land assessment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan, households farming elsewhere paid poll tax at registration and land tax where they cultivated.

sentences.zh: 漫散之戶逃於河南等路者，依見居民戶納稅。

translations.literal: Scattered households who fled to Henan and other circuits paid tax as resident households.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered refugees in Henan and elsewhere paid tax as local residents.

sentences.zh: 八年，又定西夏中興路、西寧州、兀剌海三處之稅，其數與前僧道同。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, taxes for Zhongxing Circuit of Xixia, Xining Prefecture, and Wulahai were also fixed at the same rates as for monks and Daoists.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Xixia's Zhongxing Circuit, Xining, and Wulahai were taxed at the monastic rate.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遂命戶部大定諸例：全科戶丁稅，每丁粟三石，驅丁粟一石，地稅每畝粟三升。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Ministry of Revenue was finally ordered to fix all regulations: full-assessment households paid poll tax of three shi per adult male and one shi per bond servant, land tax three sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the Ministry of Revenue fixed rates: full households paid three shi poll tax per adult male, one per bond servant, and three sheng land tax per mu.

sentences.zh: 減半科戶丁稅，每丁粟一石。

translations.literal: Half-assessment households: poll tax one shi per adult male.
translations.idiomatic: Half-assessment households paid one shi poll tax per adult male.

sentences.zh: 新收交參戶，第一年五斗，第三年一石二斗五升，第四年一石五斗，第五年一石七斗五升，第六年入丁稅。

translations.literal: Newly registered transfer households: first year five dou, third year one shi two dou five sheng, fourth year one shi five dou, fifth year one shi seven dou five sheng, sixth year entered full poll tax.
translations.idiomatic: New transfer households paid rising amounts over six years before reaching full poll tax.

sentences.zh: 協濟戶丁稅，每丁粟一石，地稅每畝粟三升。

translations.literal: Assistance households: poll tax one shi per adult male, land tax three sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Assistance households paid one shi poll tax per adult male and three sheng land tax per mu.

sentences.zh: 隨路近倉輸粟，遠倉每粟一石，折納輕賫鈔二兩。

translations.literal: Deliver to nearby circuit granaries; for distant granaries each shi of grain might be commuted to two liang of light-load notes.
translations.idiomatic: Grain went to nearby granaries; distant deliveries could be commuted at two liang of notes per shi.

sentences.zh: 富戶輸遠倉，下戶輸近倉，郡縣各差正官一員部之，每石帶納鼠耗三升，分例四升。

translations.literal: Wealthy households delivered to distant granaries, lower households to nearby ones; each prefecture and county sent one chief official to supervise; per shi three sheng mouse-loss and four sheng division allowance were added.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households delivered to distant granaries, poor ones to nearby; officials supervised collection, with three sheng mouse-loss and four sheng division allowance per shi.

sentences.zh: 凡糧到倉，以時收受，出給朱錢。

translations.literal: When grain reached the granary, it was received on schedule and red receipts issued.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries received grain on schedule and issued stamped receipts.

sentences.zh: 權勢之徒結攬稅石者罪之，仍令倍輸其數。

translations.literal: Powerful persons who monopolized tax grain were punished and made to pay double.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful monopolizers of tax grain were punished and required to pay double.

sentences.zh: 倉官、攢典、鬥腳人等飛鈔作弊者，並置諸法。

translations.literal: Granary officials, clerks, measurers, and others who committed flying-note fraud were all subject to statutory penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Granary officials, clerks, and measurers who committed receipt fraud faced statutory penalties.

sentences.zh: 輸納之期，分為三限：初限十月，中限十一月，末限十二月。

translations.literal: Payment periods were divided into three deadlines: first deadline the tenth month, middle the eleventh, final the twelfth.
translations.idiomatic: Payment was divided into three deadlines: October, November, and December.

sentences.zh: 違者，初犯笞四十，再犯杖八十。

translations.literal: Violators: first offense thirty blows with the rod, second offense eighty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Late payment brought thirty blows on first offense and eighty strokes on second.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德六年，申明稅糧條例，復定上都、河間輸納之期：上都，初限次年五月，中限六月，末限七月。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chengzong's Dade reign, grain-tax regulations were reiterated and delivery periods for Shangdu and Hejian were fixed: Shangdu—first deadline fifth month of the following year, middle sixth, final seventh; Hejian—first deadline ninth month, middle tenth, final eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dade, schedules were fixed: Shangdu paid May through July of the following year; Hejian paid September through November.

sentences.zh: 河間，初限九月，中限十月，末限十一月。

translations.literal: Hejian: first deadline ninth month, middle tenth, final eleventh.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian: September, October, and November.

sentences.zh: 秋稅、夏稅之法，行於江南。

translations.literal: The methods of autumn and summer tax were implemented in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn and summer taxes applied in the south.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖平宋時，除江東、浙西，其餘獨征秋稅而已。

translations.literal: At first, when Shizu pacified Song, apart from Jiangdong and Jiangxi, only autumn tax was levied.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai conquered Song, only autumn tax was levied outside Jiangdong and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，用姚元之請，命江南稅糧依宋舊例，折輸綿絹雜物。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, at Yao Yuanzhi's request, Jiangnan grain tax was ordered to follow the Song old example, commuted to cotton, silk, and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, at Yao Yuanzhi's request, southern grain tax followed Song practice and could be paid in silk and goods.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，又用耿左丞言，令輸米三之一，余並人鈔以折焉。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year, at Vice Chancellor Geng's suggestion, one-third was ordered paid in rice and the remainder converted to notes.
translations.idiomatic: That February, at Vice Chancellor Geng's suggestion, one-third was paid in rice and the rest in paper money.

sentences.zh: 以七百萬錠為率，歲得羨鈔十四萬錠。

translations.literal: Taking seven million ingots as the rate, fourteen thousand ingots of surplus notes were obtained annually.
translations.idiomatic: At a rate of seven million ingots, the treasury gained fourteen thousand surplus ingots annually.

sentences.zh: 其輸米者，止用宋斗斛，蓋以宋一石當今七斗故也。

translations.literal: Those paying rice used only the Song dou and hu, for one Song shi equaled seven of today's shi.
translations.idiomatic: Rice payments used the Song bushel, one Song shi equaling seven of the Yuan measure.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，又命江淮寺觀田，宋舊有者免租，續置者輸稅，其法亦可謂寬矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, temple and monastery lands in Jianghuai that had existed under Song were rent-exempt; newly acquired lands paid tax—a lenient law indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year Jianghuai temple lands held under Song were rent-exempt; newly acquired lands were taxed—a lenient rule.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞二年，始定征江南夏稅之制。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengzong's Yuanzhen reign, the system of levying Jiangnan summer tax was first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanzhen, the Jiangnan summer tax was first standardized.

sentences.zh: 於是秋稅止命輸租，夏稅則輸以木綿布絹絲綿等物。

translations.literal: Thereupon autumn tax was ordered paid only as rent, while summer tax was paid in cotton, cloth, silk, and floss.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn tax was paid in grain alone; summer tax in cotton, cloth, silk, and floss.

sentences.zh: 其所輸之數，視糧以為差。

translations.literal: The amount paid varied according to the grain assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax amounts varied with the grain assessment.

sentences.zh: 糧一石或輸鈔三貫、二貫、一貫，或一貫五百文、一貫七百文。

translations.literal: Per shi of grain one might pay three, two, or one ingot of notes, or one ingot five hundred or one ingot seven hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: Per shi of assessed grain, payment ranged from one to three ingots of notes, or one ingot plus five hundred or seven hundred wen.

sentences.zh: 輸三貫者，若江浙省婺州等路、江西省龍興等路是已。

translations.literal: Those paying three ingots included circuits such as Wuzhou in Jiangzhe and Longxing in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Three-ingot rates applied in circuits such as Wuzhou in Jiangzhe and Longxing in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 輸二貫者，若福建省泉州等五路是已。

translations.literal: Those paying two ingots included five circuits such as Quanzhou in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Two-ingot rates applied in five Fujian circuits including Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 輸一貫五百文者，若江浙省紹興路、福建省漳州等五路是已。

translations.literal: Those paying one ingot five hundred wen included Shaoxing in Jiangzhe and five circuits such as Zhangzhou in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: One ingot five hundred wen applied in Shaoxing and five Fujian circuits including Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 皆因其地利之宜，人民之眾，酌其中數而取之。

translations.literal: All took a middle figure according to local suitability and population density.
translations.idiomatic: Rates reflected local conditions and population, set at a middle figure.

sentences.zh: 其折輸之物，各隨時估之高下以為直，獨湖廣則異於是。

translations.literal: Commuted goods were valued at current market prices; only Huguang differed.
translations.idiomatic: Commuted goods were valued at market prices, except in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 初，阿裏海牙克湖廣時，罷宋夏稅，依中原例，改科門攤，每戶一貫二錢，蓋視夏稅增鈔五萬餘錠矣。

translations.literal: At first, when Alihaiya conquered Huguang, Song summer tax was abolished and the central plains door-levy of one ingot two qian per household was adopted, increasing notes by more than fifty thousand ingots over summer tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Alihaiya conquered Huguang he abolished Song summer tax and imposed a door-levy of one ingot two qian per household, raising revenue by over fifty thousand ingots.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，宣慰張國紀請科夏稅，於是湖、湘重罹其害。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, Pacification Commissioner Zhang Guoji requested summer tax; thus Hunan and Hubei suffered again.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade Zhang Guoji restored summer tax, bringing new hardship to Hunan and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 俄詔罷之。

translations.literal: Soon an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon abolished it.

sentences.zh: 三年，又改門攤為夏稅而並征之，每石計三貫四錢之上，視江浙、江西為差重云。

translations.literal: In the third year, the door-levy was changed to summer tax and levied together, more than three ingots four qian per shi—heavier than Jiangzhe and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the door-levy became summer tax, levied at over three ingots four qian per shi—heavier than Jiangzhe and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 其在官之田，許民佃種輸租。

translations.literal: Official lands might be rented by the people with rent paid.
translations.idiomatic: Official land could be leased to cultivators who paid rent.

sentences.zh: 江北、兩淮等處荒閑之地，第三年始輸。

translations.literal: Waste land in Jiangbei, Lianghuai, and elsewhere began paying tax in the third year.
translations.idiomatic: Waste land in Jiangbei and Lianghuai began paying tax in the third year of cultivation.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，又以地廣人稀更優一年，令第四年納稅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, because the land was vast and people sparse, one more year of grace was granted, tax beginning in the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dade, sparsely settled regions received another year of grace before paying in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 凡官田，夏稅皆不科。

translations.literal: All official land was exempt from summer tax.
translations.idiomatic: Official land paid no summer tax.

sentences.zh: 泰定之初，又有所謂助役糧者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding, there was also what was called assistance-grain.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taiding reign came the assistance-grain levy.

sentences.zh: 其法命江南民戶有田一頃之上者，於所輸稅外，每頃量出助役之田，具書於冊，里正以次掌之，歲收其入，以助充役之費。

translations.literal: The law ordered Jiangnan households with one qing of land or more, beyond tax paid, to set aside assistance fields per qing, recorded in registers and managed in turn by ward heads; annual income assisted corvée expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan households with one qing or more set aside assistance fields per qing, recorded and managed by ward heads, whose income funded corvée.

sentences.zh: 凡寺觀田，除宋舊額，其餘亦驗其多寡令出田助役焉。

translations.literal: All temple lands, beyond Song quotas, were also assessed by quantity to provide assistance fields.
translations.idiomatic: Temple lands beyond Song quotas were likewise required to provide assistance fields proportional to their holdings.

sentences.zh: 民賴以不困，因並著於此云。

translations.literal: The people were thereby not distressed; this is therefore recorded here as well.
translations.idiomatic: The people were spared distress, and the system is recorded here.

sentences.zh: 天下歲入糧數，總計一千二百十一萬四千七百八石。

translations.literal: Annual grain revenue empire-wide totaled 12,114,708 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide annual grain revenue totaled 12,114,708 shi.

sentences.zh: 腹裏，二百二十七萬一千四百四十九石。

translations.literal: Metropolitan region: 2,271,449 shi.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan region: 2,271,449 shi.

sentences.zh: 行省，九百八十四萬三千二百五十八石。

translations.literal: Branch secretariats: 9,843,258 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Branch secretariats: 9,843,258 shi.

sentences.zh: 遼陽省七萬二千六十六石。

translations.literal: Liaoyang Secretariat: 72,066 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang Secretariat: 72,066 shi.

sentences.zh: 河南省二百五十九萬一千二百六十九石。

translations.literal: Henan Secretariat: 2,591,269 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Secretariat: 2,591,269 shi.

sentences.zh: 陜西省二十二萬九千二十三石。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Secretariat: 229,023 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Secretariat: 229,023 shi.

sentences.zh: 四川省一十一萬六千五百七十四石。

translations.literal: Sichuan Secretariat: 116,574 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Secretariat: 116,574 shi.

sentences.zh: 甘肅省六萬五百八十六石。

translations.literal: Gansu Secretariat: 60,586 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu Secretariat: 60,586 shi.

sentences.zh: 雲南省二十七萬七千七百一十九石。

translations.literal: Yunnan Secretariat: 277,719 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan Secretariat: 277,719 shi.

sentences.zh: 江浙省四百四十九萬四千七百八十三石。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe Secretariat: 4,494,783 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe Secretariat: 4,494,783 shi.

sentences.zh: 江西省一百一十五萬七千四百四十八石。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Secretariat: 1,157,448 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Secretariat: 1,157,448 shi.

sentences.zh: 湖廣省八十四萬三千七百八十七石。

translations.literal: Huguang Secretariat: 843,787 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Secretariat: 843,787 shi.

sentences.zh: 江南三省天歷元年夏稅鈔數，總計中統鈔一十四萬九千二百七十三錠三十三貫。

translations.literal: Summer-tax note revenue for the three Jiangnan provinces in the first year of Tianli totaled 149,273 ingots and 33 guan of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: Summer-tax note revenue for the three southern provinces in Tianli year one totaled 149,273 ingots and 33 guan of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 江浙省五萬七千八百三十錠四十貫。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe Secretariat: 57,830 ingots and 40 guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe Secretariat: 57,830 ingots and 40 guan.

sentences.zh: 江西省五萬二千八百九十五錠一十一貫。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Secretariat: 52,895 ingots and 11 guan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Secretariat: 52,895 ingots and 11 guan.

sentences.zh: 湖廣省一萬九千三百七十八錠二貫。

translations.literal: Huguang Secretariat: 19,378 ingots and 2 guan.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Secretariat: 19,378 ingots and 2 guan.

sentences.zh: ○科差

translations.literal: ○ Corvée Levies
translations.idiomatic: ○ Corvée Levies

sentences.zh: 科差之名有二，曰絲料，曰包銀，其法各驗其戶之上下而科焉。

translations.literal: Corvée levies had two names: silk levy and wrapped silver; each was assessed according to household rank.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée levies took two forms, silk levy and wrapped silver, each assessed by household rank.

sentences.zh: 絲料之法，太宗丙申年始行之。

translations.literal: The silk-levy method began in Taizong's bingshen year.
translations.idiomatic: The silk levy began in Ögedei's bingshen year.

sentences.zh: 每二戶出絲一斤，並隨路絲線、顏色輸於官；

translations.literal: Every two households contributed one jin of silk, with route silk thread and dyes delivered to the government;
translations.idiomatic: Every two households contributed one jin of silk with route-specified thread and dyes to the government;

sentences.zh: 五戶出絲一斤，並隨路絲線、顏色輸於本位。

translations.literal: five households contributed one jin of silk, with route silk thread and dyes delivered to the local office.
translations.idiomatic: five households contributed one jin with thread and dyes to the local office.

sentences.zh: 包銀之法，憲宗乙卯年始定之。

translations.literal: The wrapped-silver method was first fixed in Xianzong's yimao year.
translations.idiomatic: Wrapped silver was first fixed in Möngke's yimao year.

sentences.zh: 初漢民科納包銀六兩，至是止征四兩，二兩輸銀，二兩折收絲絹、顏色等物。

translations.literal: At first Han people paid six liang of wrapped silver; now only four liang were levied—two liang in silver, two liang commuted to silk, gauze, dyes, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Han households had paid six liang; now four were levied—two in silver, two in silk, gauze, and dyes.

sentences.zh: 逮及世祖，而其制益詳。

translations.literal: When this reached Shizu, the system grew more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai the system grew more detailed.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，立十路宣撫司，定戶籍科差條例。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, ten-circuit pacification commissions were established and household corvée regulations fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, ten pacification commissions were established and corvée household regulations fixed.

sentences.zh: 然其戶大抵不一，有元管戶、交參戶、漏籍戶、協濟戶。

translations.literal: Yet households were generally not uniform: there were original households, transfer households, omitted-register households, and assistance households.
translations.idiomatic: Households were not uniform: original, transfer, omitted-register, and assistance households.

sentences.zh: 於諸戶之中，又有絲銀全科戶、減半科戶、止納絲戶、止納鈔戶；

translations.literal: Among all households, there were also silk-and-silver full-assessment households, half-assessment households, silk-only households, and note-only households;
translations.idiomatic: Among registered households there were also full-assessment silk-and-silver households, half-assessment households, silk-only households, and note-only households;

sentences.zh: 外又有攤絲戶、儲也速<角┦>兒所管納絲戶、復業戶，並漸成丁戶。

translations.literal: Besides these there were also apportioned-silk households, silk-paying households under Yesüder's jurisdiction, re-established households, and gradually adult households.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these were apportioned-silk households, silk-paying households under Prince Yesüder, households returning to cultivation, and households whose sons were gradually coming of age.

sentences.zh: 戶既不等，數亦不同。

translations.literal: Households being unequal, the amounts also differed.
translations.idiomatic: Because households were not uniform, the levies differed as well.

sentences.zh: 元管戶內，絲銀全科系官戶，每戶輸系官絲一斤六兩四錢、包銀四兩；

translations.literal: Within original households, silk-and-silver full-assessment government-silk households—each household paid government silk one jin six liang four qian and wrapped silver four liang;
translations.idiomatic: Among original households, full-assessment silk-and-silver government-silk households paid one jin six liang four qian of government silk and four liang of wrapped silver per household;

sentences.zh: 全科系官五戶絲戶，每戶輸系官絲一斤、五戶絲六兩四錢，包銀之數與系官戶同；

translations.literal: Full-assessment government-silk five-household-silk households—each household paid government silk one jin and five-household silk six liang four qian; wrapped silver was the same as for government-silk households;
translations.idiomatic: Full-assessment government-silk five-household-silk households paid one jin of government silk and six liang four qian of five-household silk per household, with wrapped silver at the same rate as government-silk households;

sentences.zh: 減半科戶，每戶輸系官絲八兩、五戶絲三兩二錢、包銀二兩；

translations.literal: Half-assessment households—each household paid government silk eight liang, five-household silk three liang two qian, and wrapped silver two liang;
translations.idiomatic: Half-assessment households paid eight liang of government silk, three liang two qian of five-household silk, and two liang of wrapped silver per household;

sentences.zh: 止納系官絲戶，若上都、隆興、西京等路十戶十斤者，每戶輸一斤，大都以南等路十戶十四斤者，每戶輸一斤六兩四錢；

translations.literal: Government-silk-only households—where ten households in circuits such as Shangdu, Longxing, and Xijing paid ten jin, each household paid one jin; where ten households in circuits south of Dadu paid fourteen jin, each household paid one jin six liang four qian;
translations.idiomatic: Government-silk-only households paid one jin per household where ten households in Shangdu, Longxing, Xijing, and similar circuits contributed ten jin, and one jin six liang four qian where ten households south of Dadu contributed fourteen jin;

sentences.zh: 止納系官五戶絲戶，每戶輸系官絲一斤、五戶絲六兩四錢。

translations.literal: Government five-household-silk-only households—each household paid government silk one jin and five-household silk six liang four qian.
translations.idiomatic: Government five-household-silk-only households paid one jin of government silk and six liang four qian of five-household silk per household.

sentences.zh: 交參戶內，絲銀戶每戶輸系官絲一斤六兩四錢、包銀四兩。

translations.literal: Within transfer households, silk-and-silver households each paid government silk one jin six liang four qian and wrapped silver four liang.
translations.idiomatic: Among transfer households, silk-and-silver households paid one jin six liang four qian of government silk and four liang of wrapped silver per household.

sentences.zh: 漏籍戶內，止納絲戶每戶輸絲之數，與交參絲銀戶同；

translations.literal: Within omitted-register households, silk-only households paid the same amount of silk as transfer silk-and-silver households;
translations.idiomatic: Among omitted-register households, silk-only households paid the same silk levy as transfer silk-and-silver households;

sentences.zh: 止納鈔戶，初年科包銀一兩五錢，次年遞增五錢，增至四兩，並科絲料。

translations.literal: Note-only households—in the first year wrapped silver of one liang five qian was levied; each succeeding year it increased by five qian up to four liang, and the silk levy was also assessed.
translations.idiomatic: Note-only households paid one liang five qian of wrapped silver the first year, increasing by five qian each year to a maximum of four liang, with the silk levy assessed as well.

sentences.zh: 協濟戶內，絲銀戶每戶輸系官絲十兩二錢、包銀四兩；

translations.literal: Within assistance households, silk-and-silver households each paid government silk ten liang two qian and wrapped silver four liang;
translations.idiomatic: Among assistance households, silk-and-silver households paid ten liang two qian of government silk and four liang of wrapped silver per household;

sentences.zh: 止納絲戶，每戶輸系官絲之數，與絲銀戶同。

translations.literal: Silk-only households—each household paid the same amount of government silk as silk-and-silver households.
translations.idiomatic: Silk-only assistance households paid the same government silk as silk-and-silver households.

sentences.zh: 攤絲戶，每戶科攤絲四斤。

translations.literal: Apportioned-silk households—each household was levied four jin of apportioned silk.
translations.idiomatic: Apportioned-silk households paid four jin of apportioned silk per household.

sentences.zh: 儲也速<角┦>兒所管戶，每戶科細絲，其數與攤絲同。

translations.literal: Households under Yesüder's jurisdiction—each household was levied fine silk in the same amount as apportioned silk.
translations.idiomatic: Households under Prince Yesüder paid fine silk at the same rate as apportioned-silk households.

sentences.zh: 復業戶並漸成丁戶，初年免科，第二年減半，第三年全科，與舊戶等。

translations.literal: Re-established households and gradually adult households were exempt the first year, paid half the second year, and paid the full assessment the third year, equal to old households.
translations.idiomatic: Re-established households and households whose sons were coming of age were exempt the first year, paid half the second, and the full levy the third, on the same terms as established households.

sentences.zh: 然絲料、包銀之外，又有俸鈔之科，其法亦以戶之高下為等，全科戶輸一兩，減半戶輸五錢。

translations.literal: Yet beyond silk levy and wrapped silver there was also the salary-note levy; this too was graded by household rank—full-assessment households paid one liang, half-assessment households five qian.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the silk levy and wrapped silver there was also a salary-note levy, graded by household rank: full-assessment households paid one liang, half-assessment households five qian.

sentences.zh: 於是以合科之數，作大門攤，分為三限輸納。

translations.literal: Thereupon the total levy was spread as a door-apportionment and divided into three installments for payment.
translations.idiomatic: The total levy was then apportioned by household and paid in three installments.

sentences.zh: 被災之地，聽輸他物折焉，其物各以時估為則。

translations.literal: In disaster-stricken areas, payment in other goods was permitted in commutation; each commodity was valued at the current market estimate.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster-stricken regions could pay in other goods at current market prices.

sentences.zh: 凡儒士及軍、站、僧、道等戶皆不與。

translations.literal: All scholar, military, relay-station, monk, and Taoist households were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and military, relay-station, monk, and Taoist households were all exempt.

sentences.zh: 二年，復定科差之期，絲料限八月，包銀初限八月，中限十月，末限十二月。

translations.literal: In the second year, corvée payment deadlines were fixed again: silk levy by the eighth month; wrapped silver in the first installment by the eighth month, the middle installment by the tenth month, and the final installment by the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year payment deadlines were reset: silk levy by the eighth month; wrapped silver in three installments due by the eighth, tenth, and twelfth months.

sentences.zh: 三年，又命絲料無過七月，包銀無過九月。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was further ordered that silk levy be paid no later than the seventh month and wrapped silver no later than the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year silk levy was due no later than the seventh month and wrapped silver no later than the ninth.

sentences.zh: 及平江南，其制益廣。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, the system grew broader still.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Jiangnan the system was greatly expanded.

sentences.zh: 至元二十八年，以《至元新格》定科差法，諸差稅皆司縣正官監視人吏置局均科。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan, the corvée method was fixed by the Zhiyuan New Statutes; all corvée taxes were evenly assessed by clerks under the supervision of the chief officials of prefecture and county, with offices established for the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan the corvée levy was codified in the Zhiyuan New Statutes, with prefectural and county officials supervising clerks who assessed levies evenly through established offices.

sentences.zh: 諸夫役皆先富強，後貧弱；

translations.literal: All labor corvées went first to the wealthy and strong, then to the poor and weak;
translations.idiomatic: All labor corvées were assigned first to wealthy households, then to poor ones;

sentences.zh: 貧富等者，先多丁，後少丁。

translations.literal: Where wealth was equal, large households came first and small households afterward.
translations.idiomatic: where wealth was equal, households with many adult males came before those with few.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德六年，又命止輸絲戶每戶科俸鈔中統鈔一兩，包銀戶每戶科二錢五分，攤絲戶每戶科攤絲五斤八兩；

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chengzong's Dade reign, it was further ordered that silk-only households be levied one liang of Zhongtong salary notes per household, wrapped-silver households two qian five fen per household, and apportioned-silk households five jin eight liang of apportioned silk per household;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dade, silk-only households were levied one liang of Zhongtong salary notes, wrapped-silver households two qian five fen, and apportioned-silk households five jin eight liang of apportioned silk per household;

sentences.zh: 絲料限八月，包銀、俸鈔限九月，布限十月。

translations.literal: Silk levy was due by the eighth month; wrapped silver and salary notes by the ninth month; cloth by the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Silk levy was due by the eighth month, wrapped silver and salary notes by the ninth, and cloth by the tenth.

sentences.zh: 大率因世祖之舊而增損云。

translations.literal: Generally it followed Shizu's old system with additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: In general the system followed Kublai's original framework with modifications.

sentences.zh: 科差總數：

translations.literal: Total corvée levies:
translations.idiomatic: Total corvée levies:

sentences.zh: 中統四年，絲七十一萬二千一百七十一斤，鈔五萬六千一百五十八百錠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong: silk 712,171 jin; notes 56,158 hundred ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongtong: 712,171 jin of silk and 56,158 ingots of notes.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，絲九十八萬六千九百一十二斤，包銀等鈔五萬六千八百七十四錠，布八萬五千四百一十二匹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan: silk 986,912 jin; wrapped silver and other notes 56,874 ingots; cloth 85,412 bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan: 986,912 jin of silk, 56,874 ingots of wrapped silver and notes, and 85,412 bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，絲一百五萬三千二百二十六斤，包銀等鈔五萬九千八十五錠。
