translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan: silk 1,053,226 jin; wrapped silver and other notes 59,085 ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan: 1,053,226 jin of silk and 59,085 ingots of wrapped silver and notes.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，絲一百九萬六千四百八十九斤，鈔七萬八千一百二十六錠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan: silk 1,096,489 jin; notes 78,126 ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan: 1,096,489 jin of silk and 78,126 ingots of notes.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，包銀差發鈔九百八十九錠，<貝八>一百一十三萬三千一百一十九索，絲一百九萬八千八百四十三斤，絹三十五萬五百三十匹，綿七萬二千一十五斤，布二十一萬一千二百二十三匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli: wrapped-silver corvée dispatch notes 989 ingots; paper currency strings 1,133,119 suo; silk 1,098,843 jin; gauze 350,530 bolts; cotton floss 72,015 jin; cloth 211,223 bolts.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianli: 989 ingots of wrapped-silver corvée notes, 1,133,119 strings of paper currency, 1,098,843 jin of silk, 350,530 bolts of gauze, 72,015 jin of cotton floss, and 211,223 bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: ○海運

translations.literal: ○ Sea Transport
translations.idiomatic: ○ Sea Transport

sentences.zh: 元都於燕，去江南極遠，而百司庶府之繁，衛士編民之眾，無不仰給於江南。

translations.literal: The Yuan capital was at Yan, extremely far from Jiangnan, yet the multitude of offices and agencies, guardsmen and registered people—all relied on Jiangnan for their supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan capital at Yan lay far from Jiangnan, yet the countless offices of government, the guards, and the common people all depended on the south for their sustenance.

sentences.zh: 自丞相伯顏獻海運之言，而江南之糧分為春夏二運。

translations.literal: From the time Chancellor Bayan presented his proposal for sea transport, Jiangnan grain was divided into spring and summer shipments.
translations.idiomatic: After Chancellor Bayan proposed sea transport, grain from Jiangnan was shipped in spring and summer convoys.

sentences.zh: 蓋至於京師者一歲多至三百萬餘石，民無挽輸之勞，國有儲蓄之富，豈非一代之良法歟！

translations.literal: In a year more than three million shi reached the capital; the people were spared the labor of hauling transport, and the state enjoyed the wealth of stored reserves—is this not an excellent method for an age!
translations.idiomatic: Each year more than three million shi reached the capital without the people's burden of overland haulage, and the state built up rich reserves—a method worthy of the age indeed!

sentences.zh: 初，伯顏平江南時，嘗命張瑄、朱清等，以宋庫藏圖籍，自崇明州從海道載入京師。

translations.literal: At first, when Bayan pacified Jiangnan, he once ordered Zhang Xuan, Zhu Qing, and others to carry Song treasury stores, maps, and archives from Chongming Prefecture by sea route into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan first pacified Jiangnan, he had Zhang Xuan and Zhu Qing transport Song treasury goods, maps, and archives from Chongming by sea to the capital.

sentences.zh: 而運糧則自浙西涉江入淮，由黃河逆水至中灤旱站，陸運至淇門，入御河，以達於京。

translations.literal: Grain transport, however, went from Zhexi across the river into the Huai, up the Yellow River against the current to the Zhongluan dry relay station, overland to Qimen, into the Imperial Canal, and so to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Grain was moved overland from Zhexi across the Yangtze into the Huai, up the Yellow River to the Zhongluan relay station, overland to Qimen, and then by the Imperial Canal to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後又開濟州泗河，自淮至新開河，由大清河至利津，河入海，因海口沙壅，又從東阿旱站運至臨清，入御河。

translations.literal: Later the Jizhou-Si River was opened; from the Huai to the Xinkai River, then by the Daqing River to Lijin, where the river entered the sea—because the estuary silted with sand, transport continued overland from the Dong'e dry relay station to Linqing and into the Imperial Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Jizhou-Si canal was opened from the Huai to the Xinkai River and then via the Daqing River to Lijin at the sea; when the estuary silted up, grain was hauled overland from Dong'e to Linqing and into the Imperial Canal.

sentences.zh: 又開膠、萊河道通海，勞費不貲，卒無成效。

translations.literal: The Jiao and Lai canal routes to the sea were also opened, but the labor and expense were beyond reckoning and in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Canals through Jiao and Lai to reach the sea were also tried, but the labor and expense were enormous and ultimately fruitless.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，伯顏追憶海道載宋圖籍之事，以為海運可行，於是請於朝廷，命上海總管羅璧、朱清、張瑄等，造平底海船六十艘，運糧四萬六千餘石，從海道至京師。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, Bayan recalled the matter of carrying Song maps and archives by sea route and judged sea transport feasible; he therefore petitioned the court and ordered Shanghai Prefect Luo Bi, Zhu Qing, Zhang Xuan, and others to build sixty flat-bottom sea ships and transport more than 46,000 shi of grain by sea route to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan Bayan recalled the sea shipment of Song archives and concluded that sea transport was viable; he petitioned the court, and Luo Bi, Zhu Qing, and Zhang Xuan built sixty flat-bottom ships and moved more than 46,000 shi of grain to the capital by sea.

sentences.zh: 然創行海洋，沿山求奧，風信失時，明年始至直沽。

translations.literal: Yet this first voyage on the open ocean hugged the coast seeking inlets, missed the seasonal winds, and did not reach Zhigu until the following year.
translations.idiomatic: On this first ocean voyage the fleet hugged the coast and missed the favorable winds, not reaching Zhigu until the following year.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷未知其利，是年十二月立京畿、江淮都漕運司二，仍各置分司，以督綱運。

translations.literal: At the time the court did not yet know its benefits; in the twelfth month of that year two capital-region and Jianghuai grain transport directorates were established, each with branch offices to supervise convoy transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court had not yet grasped the benefits; that December two grain transport directorates were set up for the capital region and Jianghuai, each with branch offices to oversee convoy shipments.

sentences.zh: 每歲令江淮漕運司運糧至中灤，京畿漕運司自中灤運至大都。

translations.literal: Each year the Jianghuai grain transport directorate was ordered to move grain to Zhongluan, and the capital-region grain transport directorate moved it from Zhongluan to Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Jianghuai directorate moved grain to Zhongluan, and the capital directorate carried it from there to Dadu.

sentences.zh: 二十年，又用王積翁議，命阿八赤等廣開新河。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, at Wang Jinweng's suggestion, Aba Chi and others were ordered to widen and open the new canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, following Wang Jinweng's proposal, Aba Chi was ordered to widen the new canal.

sentences.zh: 然新河候潮以入，船多損壞，民亦苦之。

translations.literal: Yet the new canal depended on the tide for entry; many ships were damaged and the people also suffered.
translations.idiomatic: But the new canal required the tide for entry, many ships were damaged, and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 而忙兀<角┦>言海運之舟悉皆至焉。

translations.literal: But Bayan reported that all the sea-transport ships had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan reported, however, that every sea-transport ship had arrived safely.

sentences.zh: 於是罷新開河，頗事海運，立萬戶府二，以朱清為中萬戶，張瑄為千戶，忙兀<角┦>為萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Xinkai River was abandoned and sea transport was pursued in earnest; two Ten-Thousand-Household Offices were established, with Zhu Qing as chief ten-thousand-household officer, Zhang Xuan as thousand-household officer, and Bayan as darughachi of the Ten-Thousand-Household Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinkai canal was then abandoned in favor of sea transport, and two Ten-Thousand-Household Offices were established, with Zhu Qing as chief officer, Zhang Xuan as thousand-household officer, and Bayan as darughachi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又分新河軍士水手及船，於揚州、平灤兩處運糧，命三省造船三千艘於濟州河運糧，猶未專於海道也。

translations.literal: Before long, soldiers, sailors, and ships from the new canal were again divided between Yangzhou and Pingluan for grain transport, and the Three Secretariats were ordered to build three thousand ships on the Jizhou River for grain transport—sea route was still not exclusive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon canal troops, sailors, and ships were split between Yangzhou and Pingluan for grain haulage, and the Three Secretariats were ordered to build three thousand ships on the Jizhou canal—sea transport was not yet the sole route.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，始立行泉府司，專掌海運，增置萬戶府二，總為四府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Maritime Transport Bureau was first established to manage sea transport exclusively; two more Ten-Thousand-Household Offices were added, four offices in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the Maritime Transport Bureau was established to manage sea transport exclusively, with two additional Ten-Thousand-Household Offices for four in total.

sentences.zh: 是年遂罷東平河運糧。

translations.literal: That year Dongping canal grain transport was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That year canal transport through Dongping was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，內外分置漕運司二。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, two grain transport directorates were established, one within and one without the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year two grain transport directorates were set up, one inside and one outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 其在外者於河西務置司，領接運海道糧事。

translations.literal: The outer one was placed at Hexiwu and oversaw receiving and forwarding sea-route grain.
translations.idiomatic: The outer directorate at Hexiwu received and forwarded grain arriving by sea.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，又用朱清、張瑄之請，並四府為都漕運萬戶府二，止令清、瑄二人掌之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, at Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan's request, the four offices were merged into two Capital Grain Transport Ten-Thousand-Household Offices, with only Qing and Xuan placed in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, at Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan's request, the four offices were merged into two capital grain transport offices under Zhu and Zhang alone.

sentences.zh: 其屬有千戶、百戶等官，分為各翼，以督歲運。

translations.literal: Their subordinates included thousand-household and hundred-household officers, divided into wings to supervise the annual transport.
translations.idiomatic: They had thousand- and hundred-household officers in subordinate wings to oversee the annual shipments.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，遣官至江浙議海運事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhi da, officials were dispatched to Jiang-Zhe to discuss sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhi da officials were sent to Jiangsu and Zhejiang to discuss sea transport.

sentences.zh: 時江東寧國、池、饒、建康等處運糧，率令海船從揚子江逆流而上。

translations.literal: At the time grain from Ningguo, Chi, Rao, Jiankang, and other places east of the river was generally sent up the Yangtze against the current in sea ships.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from Ningguo, Chi, Rao, Jiankang, and other districts east of the river was generally sent up the Yangtze against the current in sea-going ships.

sentences.zh: 江水湍急，又多石磯，走沙漲淺，糧船俱壞，歲歲有之。

translations.literal: The river water was swift, there were many rocky shoals, shifting sand and shoaling shallows—and grain ships were wrecked every year.
translations.idiomatic: The current was swift, the river strewn with rocky shoals and shifting sandbars, and grain ships were wrecked every year.

sentences.zh: 又湖廣、江西之糧運至真州泊入海船，船大底小，亦非江中所宜。

translations.literal: Moreover, grain from Huguang and Jiangxi was transported to Zhenzhou and berthed in sea ships—broad above and narrow below, ill suited to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from Huguang and Jiangxi was brought to Zhenzhou and loaded onto sea ships whose broad decks and narrow hulls were unsuited to the river.

sentences.zh: 於是以嘉興、松江秋糧，並江淮、江浙財賦府歲辦糧充運。

translations.literal: Thereupon autumn grain from Jiaxing and Songjiang, together with the annual grain prepared by the Jiang-Huai and Jiang-Zhe revenue offices, was used to fill the shipments.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn grain from Jiaxing and Songjiang and the annual grain levied by the Jiang-Huai and Jiang-Zhe revenue offices were then used to supply the convoys.

sentences.zh: 海漕之利，蓋至是博矣。

translations.literal: The benefits of sea transport had by then become fully broad indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The benefits of sea transport were by then fully realized.

sentences.zh: 凡運糧，每石有腳價鈔。

translations.literal: For all grain transport, each shi had a transport-fee in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Each shi of transported grain carried a freight allowance paid in notes.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年，給中統鈔八兩五錢，其後遞減至於六兩五錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan, eight liang five qian of Zhongtong notes were paid; afterward this was progressively reduced to six liang five qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan the allowance was eight liang five qian of Zhongtong notes, later reduced step by step to six liang five qian.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，以福建、浙東船戶至平江載糧者，道遠費廣，通增為至元鈔一兩六錢，香糯一兩七錢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhi da, because ship-owning households from Fujian and eastern Zhejiang who carried grain to Pingjiang faced long routes and heavy expenses, the allowance was uniformly raised to one liang six qian of Zhiyuan notes for ordinary grain and one liang seven qian for fragrant glutinous rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhi da, because Fujian and eastern Zhejiang shipowners hauling grain to Pingjiang faced long routes and heavy costs, the allowance was raised to one liang six qian of Zhiyuan notes for ordinary grain and one liang seven qian for fragrant glutinous rice.

sentences.zh: 四年，又增為二兩，香糯二兩八錢，稻谷一兩四錢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, it was further raised to two liang; fragrant glutinous rice two liang eight qian; husked paddy one liang four qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the rate rose to two liang for ordinary grain, two liang eight qian for fragrant glutinous rice, and one liang four qian for husked paddy.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，斟酌遠近，復增其價。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yan you, weighing distance near and far, the price was again increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yan you rates were raised again according to distance.

sentences.zh: 福建船運糙粳米每石一十三兩，溫、臺、慶元船運糙粳、香糯每石一十一兩五錢，紹興、浙西船每石一十一兩，白粳價同，稻谷每石八兩，黑豆每石依糙白糧例給焉。

translations.literal: Fujian ships transporting coarse regular rice received thirteen liang per shi; Wen, Tai, and Qingyuan ships transporting coarse regular and fragrant glutinous rice received eleven liang five qian per shi; Shaoxing and western Zhe ships received eleven liang per shi, white regular rice at the same rate; husked paddy eight liang per shi; black beans paid on the same principle as coarse and white grain.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian ships carrying coarse regular rice received thirteen liang per shi; Wenzhou, Taizhou, and Qingyuan ships carrying coarse regular and fragrant glutinous rice received eleven liang five qian; Shaoxing and western Zhejiang ships received eleven liang, with white regular rice at the same rate; husked paddy eight liang; black beans at the same rate as coarse and white grain.

sentences.zh: 初，海運之道，自平江劉家港入海，經揚州路通州海門縣黃連沙頭、萬里長灘開洋，沿山奧而行，抵淮安路鹽城縣，歷西海州、海寧府東海縣、密州、膠州界，放靈山洋投東北，路多淺沙，行月餘始抵成山。

translations.literal: At first the sea-transport route entered the sea from Liu Family Port in Pingjiang, passed Huangliansha Point and Wanli Changtan at Tongzhou's Haimen County in Yangzhou Circuit, sailed the open sea, hugged coastal inlets to Yancheng County in Huai'an Circuit, crossed the borders of Xihai Prefecture, Donghai County in Haining Prefecture, Mizhou, and Jiaozhou, entered Lingshan Ocean toward the northeast—shallow sand abounded along the way, and more than a month passed before reaching Chengshan.
translations.idiomatic: The original sea route departed from Liu Family Port in Pingjiang, passed Huangliansha and Wanli Changtan off Tongzhou's Haimen County, sailed the open sea along coastal inlets to Yancheng in Huai'an, then through Xihai, Donghai in Haining, Mizhou, and Jiaozhou, and entered Lingshan Ocean toward the northeast; shallow sandbanks made the passage slow, and more than a month passed before reaching Chengshan.

sentences.zh: 計其水程，自上海至楊村馬頭，凡一萬三千三百五十里。

translations.literal: Calculating the water distance from Shanghai to Yangcun Matou, it totaled 13,350 li.
translations.idiomatic: The water distance from Shanghai to Yangcun Matou totaled 13,350 li.

sentences.zh: 至元二十九年，朱清等言其路險惡，復開生道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan, Zhu Qing and others said the route was dangerous and treacherous, and a living route was opened anew.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Zhiyuan Zhu Qing reported that the route was perilous, and a new direct route was opened.

sentences.zh: 自劉家港開洋，至撐腳沙轉沙觜，至三沙、洋子江，過匾擔沙、大洪，又過萬里長灘，放大洋至青水洋，又經黑水洋至成山，過劉島，至芝罘、沙門二島，放萊州大洋，抵界河口，其道差為徑直。

translations.literal: From Liu Family Port it entered the open sea, turned at Chengjiao Sha and Shazui, reached Sansha and Yangzi River, passed Biandan Sha and Dahong, crossed Wanli Changtan again, entered the broad ocean to Qingshui Ocean, then crossed Heishui Ocean to Chengshan, passed Liudao, reached the two islands of Zhifu and Shamen, entered Laizhou Ocean, and arrived at Jiehe mouth—the route was somewhat more direct.
translations.idiomatic: From Liu Family Port the fleet sailed the open sea to Chengjiao Sha and Shazui, then to Sansha and Yangzi River, past Biandan Sha and Dahong and again across Wanli Changtan, out to Qingshui Ocean and through Heishui Ocean to Chengshan, past Liudao to Zhifu and Shamen islands, into Laizhou Ocean, and to Jiehe mouth—a somewhat more direct route.

sentences.zh: 明年，千戶殷明略又開新道，從劉家港入海，至崇明州三沙放洋，向東行，入黑水大洋，取成山轉西至劉家島，又至登州沙門島，於萊州大洋入界河。

translations.literal: The next year, Thousand-Household Officer Yin Minglue opened yet another new route: from Liu Family Port into the sea, entering the open ocean at Sansha in Chongming Prefecture, sailing east, entering Heishui Ocean, taking Chengshan and turning west to Liujia Island, then reaching Shamen Island in Dengzhou, and entering Jiehe from Laizhou Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Thousand-Household Officer Yin Minglue opened another route: from Liu Family Port to the open sea at Sansha in Chongming, east into Heishui Ocean, west past Chengshan to Liujia Island, then to Shamen Island off Dengzhou, and into Jiehe from Laizhou Ocean.

sentences.zh: 當舟行風信有時，自浙西至京師，不過旬日而已，視前二道為最便云。

translations.literal: When ships sailed with timely winds, from western Zhe to the capital took no more than ten days—said to be the most convenient of the three routes.
translations.idiomatic: With favorable winds the passage from western Zhejiang to the capital took no more than ten days—the most convenient of the three routes.

sentences.zh: 然風濤不測，糧船漂溺者無歲無之，間亦有船壞而棄其米者。

translations.literal: Yet winds and waves were unpredictable; grain ships lost to drifting and drowning occurred every year without fail, and sometimes ships were wrecked and their rice abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet winds and waves were unpredictable; grain ships were lost every year, and sometimes wrecked ships forced crews to jettison their cargo.

sentences.zh: 至元二十三年始責償於運官，人船俱溺者乃免。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan, compensation was first required of transport officers; only when both men and ships were drowned was one exempt.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan transport officers were first held liable for losses; only total loss of men and ships brought exemption.

sentences.zh: 然視河漕之費，則其所得蓋多矣。

translations.literal: Yet compared with the expense of canal transport, the gain was much the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, compared with canal transport the savings were considerable.

sentences.zh: ○鈔法

translations.literal: ○ Paper Currency
translations.idiomatic: ○ Paper Currency

sentences.zh: 鈔始於唐之飛錢、宋之交會、金之交鈔。

translations.literal: Paper notes began with the Tang's flying money, the Song's exchange certificates, and the Jin's exchange notes.
translations.idiomatic: Paper currency originated in the Tang flying-money system, the Song exchange certificates, and the Jin exchange notes.

sentences.zh: 其法以物為母，鈔為子，子母相權而行，即《周官》質劑之意也。

translations.literal: Its method takes goods as the standard and notes as the token; mother and token mutually measure each other in circulation—this is the meaning of the Zhou Offices' pledge certificates.
translations.idiomatic: The principle treats commodities as the standard and notes as tokens; the two mutually measure value in circulation—much like the pledge certificates described in the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 元初仿唐、宋、金之法，有行用鈔，其制無文籍可考。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, following the Tang, Song, and Jin systems, there were circulating notes, but their regulations cannot be verified in any surviving record.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuan the dynasty followed Tang, Song, and Jin precedents and issued circulating notes, though no written regulations survive to document the original system.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，始造交鈔，以絲為本。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, exchange notes were first produced, with silk as their basis.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, Kublai Khan first issued exchange notes backed by silk.

sentences.zh: 每銀五十兩易絲鈔一千兩，諸物之直，並從絲例。

translations.literal: For every fifty taels of silver one exchanged one thousand taels of silk notes; the value of all goods likewise followed the silk standard.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty taels of silver could be exchanged for one thousand taels of silk notes, and the prices of all goods were reckoned on the same silk standard.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，又造中統元寶鈔。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, Zhongtong yuanbao notes were also produced.
translations.idiomatic: That October the government also issued Zhongtong yuanbao notes.

sentences.zh: 其文以十計者四：曰一十文、二十文、三十文、五十文。

translations.literal: Those denominated by tens were four in number: ten wen, twenty wen, thirty wen, and fifty wen.
translations.idiomatic: There were four denominations counted in tens: ten, twenty, thirty, and fifty wen.

sentences.zh: 以百計者三：曰一百文、二百文、五百文。

translations.literal: Those denominated by hundreds were three: one hundred wen, two hundred wen, and five hundred wen.
translations.idiomatic: Three were counted in hundreds: one hundred, two hundred, and five hundred wen.

sentences.zh: 以貫計者二：曰一貫文、二貫文。

translations.literal: Those denominated by guan were two: one guan and two guan.
translations.idiomatic: Two were counted in guan: one guan and two guan.

sentences.zh: 每一貫同交鈔一兩，兩貫同白銀一兩。

translations.literal: Each one guan equaled one liang of exchange notes; two guan equaled one liang of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: One guan was equivalent to one liang of exchange notes, and two guan to one liang of silver.

sentences.zh: 又以文綾織為中統銀貨。

translations.literal: Patterned silk was also woven into Zhongtong silver tokens.
translations.idiomatic: The government also wove patterned silk into Zhongtong silver tokens.

sentences.zh: 其等有五：曰一兩、二兩、三兩、五兩、十兩。

translations.literal: Their denominations were five: one liang, two liang, three liang, five liang, and ten liang.
translations.idiomatic: These came in five denominations: one, two, three, five, and ten liang.

sentences.zh: 每一兩同白銀一兩，而銀貨蓋未及行云。

translations.literal: Each one liang equaled one liang of white silver, but the silver tokens probably never entered circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Each token liang was pegged to one liang of silver, but the silver tokens apparently never entered general circulation.

sentences.zh: 五年，設各路平準庫，主平物價，使相依準，不至低昂，仍給鈔一萬二千錠，以為鈔本。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, equalization treasuries were established in each circuit to stabilize prices, keep them mutually aligned, and prevent sharp rises and falls; twelve thousand ingots of notes were also supplied as note reserve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year equalization treasuries were set up in every circuit to stabilize prices and keep them from swinging too high or too low, and twelve thousand ingots of notes were allocated as reserve backing.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，添造釐鈔。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, fractional notes were added to production.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan the government began issuing fractional notes.

sentences.zh: 其例有三：曰二文、三文、五文。

translations.literal: Their denominations were three: two wen, three wen, and five wen.
translations.idiomatic: These came in three denominations: two, three, and five wen.

sentences.zh: 初，鈔印用木為版，十三年鑄銅易之。

translations.literal: At first wooden blocks were used to print notes; in the thirteenth year copper plates replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: Notes were first printed from wooden blocks; in the thirteenth year copper plates were cast to replace them.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以厘鈔不便於民，復命罷印。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, because fractional notes were inconvenient for the people, an order was again issued to stop printing them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year fractional notes were judged inconvenient for the public, and printing was ordered stopped.

sentences.zh: 然元寶、交鈔行之既久，物重鈔輕。

translations.literal: Yet after the yuanbao and exchange notes had circulated for a long time, goods grew heavy and notes grew light.
translations.idiomatic: After the yuanbao and exchange notes had circulated for many years, however, commodities retained their value while the notes depreciated.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遂改造至元鈔，自二貫至五文，凡十有一等，與中統鈔通行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Zhiyuan notes were therefore reissued, from two guan down to five wen—eleven denominations in all—and circulated together with Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year the government therefore reissued Zhiyuan notes in eleven denominations from two guan down to five wen, and these circulated alongside Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 每一貫文當中統鈔五貫文。

translations.literal: Each one guan of Zhiyuan notes equaled five guan of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: One guan of Zhiyuan notes was worth five guan of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 依中統之初，隨路設立官庫，貿易金銀，平準鈔法。

translations.literal: Following the practice at the beginning of Zhongtong, official treasuries were established in each circuit to trade gold and silver and stabilize the note system.
translations.idiomatic: As at the start of Zhongtong, official treasuries were established in each circuit to exchange gold and silver and keep the note system in balance.

sentences.zh: 每花銀一兩，入庫其價至元鈔二貫，出庫二貫五分，赤金一兩，入庫二十貫，出庫二十貫五百文。

translations.literal: For each liang of patterned silver deposited, the treasury price was two guan of Zhiyuan notes; on withdrawal, two guan five fen; for each liang of red gold deposited, twenty guan on deposit and twenty guan five hundred wen on withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned silver was bought at two guan of Zhiyuan notes per liang and sold at two guan five fen; red gold was bought at twenty guan per liang and sold at twenty guan five hundred wen.

sentences.zh: 偽造鈔者處死，首告者賞鈔五錠，仍以犯人家產給之。

translations.literal: Counterfeiters of notes were punished with death; informants were rewarded with five ingots of notes, and the offender's household property was also given to them.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting notes was punishable by death; informants received five ingots of notes plus the counterfeiter's household property.

sentences.zh: 其法為最善。

translations.literal: This system was the most excellent.
translations.idiomatic: This was the soundest of the note systems.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，武宗復以物重鈔輕，改造至大銀鈔，自二兩至二厘定為一十三等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, Wuzong again, because goods were heavy and notes light, reissued Zhida silver notes, fixed at thirteen denominations from two liang down to two li.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida, because commodities again outweighed the notes in value, Wuzong reissued Zhida silver notes in thirteen denominations from two liang down to two li.

sentences.zh: 每一兩準至元鈔五貫，白銀一兩，赤金一錢。

translations.literal: Each one liang equaled five guan of Zhiyuan notes, one liang of white silver, and one qian of red gold.
translations.idiomatic: One liang of Zhida silver notes was equivalent to five guan of Zhiyuan notes, one liang of silver, or one qian of gold.

sentences.zh: 元之鈔法，至是蓋三變矣。

translations.literal: The Yuan's note system had by this point changed three times in all.
translations.idiomatic: By this point the Yuan note system had undergone three major reforms.

sentences.zh: 大抵至元鈔五倍於中統，至大鈔又五倍於至元。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, Zhiyuan notes were five times Zhongtong notes, and Zhida notes were again five times Zhiyuan notes.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, Zhiyuan notes were valued at five times Zhongtong notes, and Zhida notes at five times Zhiyuan notes.

sentences.zh: 然未及期年，仁宗即位，以倍數太多，輕重失宜，遂有罷銀鈔之詔。

translations.literal: Yet before a full year had passed, Renzong acceded to the throne; because the multiples were too great and the weight of value was ill suited, an edict was issued abolishing the silver notes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before a full year had passed Renzong succeeded to the throne, judged the exchange multiples excessive and the weight of value ill balanced, and issued an edict abolishing the silver notes.

sentences.zh: 而中統、至元二鈔，終元之世，蓋常行焉。

translations.literal: Yet the two note issues, Zhongtong and Zhiyuan, remained in regular circulation throughout the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongtong and Zhiyuan notes, however, remained in regular circulation throughout the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 凡鈔之昏爛者，至元二年，委官就交鈔庫，以新鈔倒換，除工墨三十文。

translations.literal: As for worn and tattered notes, in the second year of Zhiyuan officials were appointed at the exchange-note treasuries to swap them for new notes, deducting thirty wen for labor and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Worn and tattered notes could be exchanged for new ones at the note treasuries; in the second year of Zhiyuan a fee of thirty wen was charged for labor and ink.

sentences.zh: 三年，減為二十文。

translations.literal: In the third year it was reduced to twenty wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the fee was reduced to twenty wen.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，復增如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year it was again increased to the former amount.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year it was raised again to the original rate.

sentences.zh: 其貫伯分明，微有破損者，並令行用，違者罪之。

translations.literal: Those whose guan and hundred denominations were clear and only slightly damaged were all ordered to be accepted in circulation; violators were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Notes whose denominations remained legible despite slight damage were all required to be accepted; refusal was punishable.

sentences.zh: 所倒之鈔，每季各路就令納課正官，解赴省部焚毀，隸行省者就焚之。

translations.literal: The notes exchanged in each season were every quarter ordered by each circuit to be sent by the revenue-collection chief official to the provincial ministry for burning; those under branch secretariats were burned on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Exchanged notes were collected each quarter by the chief revenue officials of each circuit and sent to the central ministry for destruction; circuits under branch secretariats burned them locally.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，戶部定昏鈔為二十五樣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, the Ministry of Revenue fixed twenty-five categories of worn notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dade the Ministry of Revenue classified worn notes into twenty-five types.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，又定焚毀之所，皆以廉訪司官監臨，隸行省者，行省官同監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding, the places of burning were also fixed; in all cases surveillance-commission officials supervised, and where branch secretariats had jurisdiction, branch-secretariat officials supervised together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiding designated burning sites were also established, all supervised by surveillance commissioners; where branch secretariats had jurisdiction, their officials supervised jointly.

sentences.zh: 其制之大略如此。

translations.literal: The general outline of the system was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general outline of the system.

sentences.zh: 若錢，自九府圜法行於成周，歷代未嘗或廢。

translations.literal: As for coin, since the Nine Treasuries round-coin system operated in the Zhou of Cheng, no dynasty ever wholly abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: Coinage, since the Nine Treasuries round-coin system of the Zhou, had never been wholly abandoned by any dynasty.

sentences.zh: 元之交鈔、寶鈔雖皆以錢為文，而錢則弗之鑄也。

translations.literal: Although the Yuan's exchange notes and treasure notes were all denominated in coin, coin itself was not cast.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yuan exchange notes and treasure notes were all denominated in coin units, the dynasty itself did not cast coin.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大三年，初行錢法，立資國院、泉貨監以領之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuzong's Zhida reign, the coin system was first implemented; the Resource-Nation Bureau and the Currency Superintendency were established to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wuzong's Zhida reign a coin system was first introduced, with a Resource-Nation Bureau and Currency Superintendency established to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 其錢曰至大通寶者，一文準至大銀鈔一厘；

translations.literal: The coin called Zhi Da tongbao: one wen equaled one li of Zhida silver notes;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhi Da tongbao coin was pegged at one wen to one li of Zhida silver notes;

sentences.zh: 曰大元通寶者，一文準至大通寶錢一十文。

translations.literal: that called Dayuan tongbao: one wen equaled ten wen of Zhi Da tongbao coin.
translations.idiomatic: the Dayuan tongbao coin at one wen to ten wen of Zhi Da tongbao coin.

sentences.zh: 歷代銅錢，悉依古例，與至大錢通用。

translations.literal: Copper coins of successive dynasties all followed ancient precedent and circulated together with Zhida coin.
translations.idiomatic: Copper coins of earlier dynasties were accepted by ancient precedent and circulated alongside Zhida coin.

sentences.zh: 其當五、當三、折二，並以舊數用之。

translations.literal: Those worth five, worth three, and discounted to two all continued to be used at their old counts.
translations.idiomatic: Coins rated at five, three, and two continued to be used at their former values.

sentences.zh: 明年，仁宗復下詔，以鼓鑄弗給，新舊資用，其弊滋甚，與銀鈔皆廢不行，所立院、監亦皆罷革，而專用至元、中統鈔云。

translations.literal: The next year Renzong again issued an edict: because minting could not supply demand and old and new currency mixed in use, the abuses grew worse; together with the silver notes all were abolished and ceased circulation, and the bureaus and superintendencies established were also abolished—only Zhiyuan and Zhongtong notes were used exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Renzong issued another edict: minting could not meet demand, old and new coin circulated together, and abuses multiplied; both coin and silver notes were abolished, the bureaus and superintendencies were dissolved, and only Zhiyuan and Zhongtong notes remained in use.

sentences.zh: 歲印鈔數：

translations.literal: Annual note printing totals:
translations.idiomatic: Annual note printing totals:

translations.idiomatic: First year of Zhongtong: 73,352 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Second year: 116,208 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Third year: 77,252 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Fourth year: 109,488 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Sixth year: 22,896 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Seventh year: 96,768 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Eighth year: 47,000 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Ninth year: 86,256 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Tenth year: 110,192 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth year: 1,419,665 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth year: 1,021,645 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth year: 1,023,400 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth year: 788,320 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth year: 1,135,800 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth year: 969,444 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, 629,904 ingots of Zhongtong notes were issued.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, 2,043,080 ingots of Zhongtong notes were issued.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, 2,181,600 ingots of Zhongtong notes were issued.

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year: 83,200 ingots of Zhongtong notes and 1,001,017 ingots of Zhiyuan notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, 83,200 ingots of Zhongtong notes and 1,001,017 ingots of Zhiyuan notes were issued.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, 1,780,093 ingots of Zhiyuan notes were issued.
